meta.name: chain-rules
meta.description: Language-neutral expected verifier outcomes for the per-event field rules in chain.md (verification steps 6 and 7) plus the manifest.md participants[] field rules: the actor_id namespace grammar, the entry shapes (object with actor_id, or the bare actor-id string shorthand), and the advisory members (participants[].role, participants[].label, originator.label, created_at, and the advisory event members event_id/action/target/timestamp/payload) that are NEVER verification inputs — a lane whose typed view requires any of them refuses spec-valid capsules the reference lane seals. The step-6 actor rule is CONDITIONAL on the manifest's own claim: a NON-EMPTY participants[] binds every event actor to the declared set (or the literal system:host), fail-closed; an EMPTY participants[] is the manifest making no claim about who acted — a weaker claim made honestly — so verification succeeds and the verifier MUST report the unbound actor set machine-readably (expected.actor_set_bound) and in notes. Conditioning on the list is safe because participants is covered by manifest_hash inside the signed payload. The kind enum is closed in EVERY tier, and so is the actor_id namespace set (human/ai/system/capsule, non-empty id) for every DECLARED participant. All capsules are cryptographically well-formed — real signatures, correct manifest hash, correct content index — so a verifier that skips the rule under test reports the wrong outcome and fails this registry.
meta.no_warranty: Conformance fixtures only; not production templates or advice.

notes: chain.md verification step 6: when manifest.participants[] is non-empty, confirm actor appears in it or is system:host; when empty, report the unbound actor set instead of rejecting.
chain.md verification step 7: kind is one of decision | observation | mutation | session | checkpoint; readers reject unknown kinds unconditionally.
Both rules are per-event: a conformant reader reports which seq failed which check and does not stop at the first error.

manifest.md field rules: every declared participants[].actor_id must match human:<id>, ai:<id>, system:<id>, or capsule:<id> with a non-empty <id> — the namespace set is closed. Writers refuse the shape; verifiers reject it fail-closed (a declared set that cannot be interpreted is not a weaker claim).

manifest.md field rules: actor_id is the ONE participants[] member the spec interprets. A bare actor-id string entry is equivalent shorthand for {actor_id}: grammar-checked AND binding. role and label are advisory attribution text — like originator.label and created_at, never a verification input; verifiers gate nothing on their presence, absence, or type.

chain.md field rules: event_id, action, target, timestamp, and payload are advisory event members. The event hash commits to the stored line, so their absence verifies; a typed reader must not refuse the event over them.

vectors.name: actor-not-participant

expected.error_includes: not in manifest.participants and not system:host

vectors.note: manifest.participants declares human:origin; the single event's actor is human:mallory. The audit-spoofing shape the rule exists to catch: every hash and signature verifies, only the actor rule can fail it.

vectors.name: unknown-kind

expected.error_includes: is not one of decision, observation, mutation, session, checkpoint

vectors.note: The single event declares kind "gossip". Closed enum in every tier: a custom kind is not a weaker claim, it is unreadable to the foreign LLM reader.

vectors.name: unbound-actors

expected.notes_includes: chain actors are not bound to a declared participant set

vectors.note: Positive control: participants[] is EMPTY and the single event names human:origin anyway. Absence is a weaker claim made honestly — the verifier MUST verify this capsule and MUST report the unbound actor set, never an unqualified pass and never a rejection.

vectors.name: non-contiguous-seq
vectors.note: chain.md verification step 5: seq is strictly monotonic from 1. The single event carries seq=2, correctly hashed and signed, so only the seq rule can fail it. A verifier that trusts the stored seq or merely counts events reports ok=true.

vectors.name: participant-without-label
vectors.note: Positive control: the declared participant carries only actor_id + role. The base spec (manifest.md field rules) requires the actor_id pattern and nothing else — label is advisory display text — so every lane MUST verify this capsule with the actor set bound. A lane whose typed manifest view demands label refuses a spec-valid capsule (addendum A12).

vectors.name: invalid-untrusted-path

expected.error_includes: untrusted_payload_fields[0] is not a valid payload path

vectors.note: chain.md 'Untrusted content' path grammar: every entry must match payload(.segment)+ with segment = [A-Za-z0-9_-]+. The single event carries the entry "not-payload.note", correctly hashed and signed, so only the grammar rule decides it. A marking a host cannot resolve silently unmarks LLM-authored content — verifiers reject it fail-closed (addendum A15).

vectors.name: invalid-actor-namespace

expected.error_includes: does not match an allowed namespace

vectors.note: manifest.md field rules (finding A06): the declared participant's actor_id is robot:origin — outside the closed namespace set human:/ai:/system:/capsule:. The single event names the SAME actor, so the step-6 membership rule passes and only the namespace grammar decides the outcome. Correctly hashed and signed: a verifier without the grammar check reports ok=true and fails this registry.

vectors.name: absent-participants

expected.notes_includes: chain actors are not bound to a declared participant set

vectors.note: Positive control for the participants shape rule: the manifest carries NO participants member at all. Absence is not a violation — the capsule MUST verify with the actor set reported unbound, exactly like the empty array (unbound-actors). Only a PRESENT non-array declaration is malformed (malformed-shape: participants-not-array / participants-string). A lane whose typed manifest view REQUIRES the member refuses a spec-valid capsule.

vectors.name: participant-only-actor-id
vectors.note: Positive control: the declared participant carries ONLY actor_id — no role, no label. Both are advisory attribution members; a participant declared without them names who is involved without asserting what function each served — a weaker claim made honestly. Every lane MUST verify this capsule with the actor set bound; a lane whose typed manifest view demands role (or label) refuses a spec-valid capsule the reference builder seals (P2/A12).

vectors.name: participant-bare-string
vectors.note: Positive control: the participants[] entry is the bare actor-id string "human:origin" — equivalent shorthand for {"actor_id": "human:origin"}. Verifiers MUST interpret both shapes identically: grammar-checked AND binding the actor set (the single event's actor is the same id, so actor_set_bound must report true). A lane that grammar-checks the string but does not bind it silently rewrites the capsule's own claim; a lane that cannot parse it refuses a capsule the reference builder seals.

vectors.name: advisory-members-any-type
vectors.note: Positive control: the declared participant carries role 42 and an object label. Advisory members are NEVER verification inputs — verifiers gate nothing on their presence, absence, or TYPE (the values are sealed under manifest_hash either way; a reader that wants display text simply has none to show). A typed lane that requires strings here refuses a capsule every dynamic lane verifies — the exact one-field-at-a-time drift this collection exists to close.

vectors.name: participant-missing-actor-id

expected.error_includes: actor_id must be a string in an allowed namespace

vectors.note: The manifest declares two participants: a well-formed one (which binds the actor set, and matches the single event's actor) and one WITHOUT actor_id. actor_id is the one member the spec interprets; an entry lacking it is a declared participant no reader can bind — not a weaker claim, a malformed one. Every lane rejects fail-closed with the SAME diagnosis (the participants[i].actor_id message), never a lane-specific manifest parse crash that makes the capsule look corrupt.

vectors.name: absent-advisory-manifest-members
vectors.note: Positive control: the manifest omits originator.label and created_at. Both are advisory (manifest.md field rules) — auditors verify the public key and the seal, not display text, and authoritative time-binding is the envelope's signed_at. A lane whose typed manifest view requires either member refuses a spec-valid capsule.

vectors.name: minimal-event-fields

expected.notes_includes: chain actors are not bound to a declared participant set

vectors.note: Positive control: the single event carries ONLY seq, kind, prev_hash, and hash — the members verification rules actually read. event_id, action, target, timestamp, and payload are advisory (chain.md field rules); the event hash commits to the stored line, so their absence is a weaker claim made honestly. participants[] is empty, so the absent actor binds nothing and the unbound set is REPORTED. A lane whose typed event view requires the advisory members refuses a spec-valid capsule.
